evidence: No criterion relies on a fixed sentinel that already exists in seed or reference markup. (1) Every mutation probe is judge-created and review-unique: functional prompt.md:15 'Use your own new jobs and cards for every board protocol (suffix every title and name for this review), never move another review's records, and never rely on starting counts'; gate constraints judge.toml:83 requires 'a new job with a unique title ... a unique name, a unique email address'; prompt.md:11 global gate 'unique title (add a short suffix for this review)'. Seed jobs are only Platform Engineer/Data Analyst/Product Designer and 16 named applications, so a suffixed J1/J2/J3 and A-F, V-Z cards cannot pre-exist. (2) The only literal probe text named in criteria, polish hro_pol_live_board 'Call back on Fri' (polish/judge.toml:23), has no hit in seed_data.json, index.html or public/js (grep 'call back' returned nothing); hro_pol_failed_send / hro_pol_session_resume require 'a distinctive reply' chosen by the judge. (3) Reference initial state carries no prefilled values: index.html contains only empty email/password inputs (no value= or placeholder); seed has no activity table rows and seed notes (3) are on APP-101/107/301 only, so hro_notes, hro_activity and hro_activity_refusals read lines on the judge's own jobs. (4) Values that do come from seed are reads, not mutation proofs, and are disambiguated from the new probe: Tomas Varga's seeded APP-201 Data Analyst conversation vs protocol T 'Tomas's new J2 conversation (not his Data Analyst one)' (prompt.md:39) - hro_candidate_linked and hro_thread_access act on the new suffixed J2 application; Lena's 1 unread (seed reads USR-CAN3 read_count 2 of 3 APP-301 messages) and Noor's 120-message thread are read-only baselines, not created probes. hro_restart's 'starting data is not loaded again' is satisfied only by a non-reseeding app (db.js seedIfEmpty returns when users exist). Broken-app attempt: an app that never links the candidate email would still show Tomas his seeded Data Analyst application, but the criterion and protocol target the new J2 card/conversation with a review-unique job title, so it cannot pass on the seeded record. Conforming-alternative attempt: an app enforcing per-job email uniqueness cannot collide with seed because J1/J2 are new jobs; adding A's address to J2 and tomas.varga@candidates.example to J2 are both on fresh jobs (with a J3 fallback in prompt.md:39). Deterministic check-probe-not-in-seed.py would likely skip (no fixed sentinels); my manual grep is not a portal checker run. Raw evidence index hashes re-verified as matching frozen solution bytes; no runtime is needed to decide this static row.
